text.brief: A satellite analyst in 2041 watches the parking lots empty at a consumer drone plant in Shenzhen and refill overnight with military trucks. The plant's motors and batteries still arrive through a trading house in Kuala Lumpur.
text.record: A Navy intelligence estimate in 2023 put mainland shipbuilding capacity at about 232 times America's ([CSIS: The Threat of China's Shipbuilding Empire](https://www.csis.org/analysis/threat-chinas-shipbuilding-empire)). The FCC added foreign-made drones and their components to its Covered List on December 22, 2025 ([FCC DA 25-1086 (Covered List)](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-25-1086A1.pdf)). Commerce suspended its rule extending export controls to affiliates of listed firms for one year in November 2025 under the trade truce ([Federal Register: one-year suspension of affiliates rule (BIS)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/11/12/2025-19846/one-year-suspension-of-expansion-of-end-user-controls-for-affiliates-of-certain-listed-entities)).
text.reading: A faction of a split Party turns civilian factories into arsenals and borrows other nations' ports and traders as its road. Each shipment moves through a third country that sees ordinary commerce. This is Stratagem 24, borrow the road to conquer Guo.
text.coreEvent: A PLA faction converts civilian drone and shipbuilding lines to war production during an internal crisis before 2046.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. Allied firms still sell the inputs that let a civilian line become a military one.
text.fix: Treat dual-use inputs to mainland mass producers as military exports and track them through third countries.
